episode.subject: Cucamonga manroot
episode.title: Below the slender stems
episode.body:
Rain washed the soil off my tuber. The part of me that had always been underground was suddenly holding a fallen leaf.

Up in the scrub, a leaf that size could pull a thin stem sideways.

I waited for the familiar tug. The leaf lay flat. That part of me did not bend.

proposals.admission: Held for mechanically predictable event without consequential response
proposals.visualReview: Exact published large image opened individually. An exposed pale-brown tuber fills the center and lower frame; rooted green stems pass above and around it, eroded soil surrounds it, and one bright green leaf rests on its broad surface. Bark-like surface cracks and old marks visible; no cause or freshness assigned to these marks. The tuber and leaf are sharp, with good separation from darker soil.
proposals.fictionBoundary: Observer explicitly reports exposure after recent rains. Leaf descent, familiar tug expected from a thin stem, and absence of perceived bending are fictional temporal and felt experience. The photo shows a resting leaf, not its fall. No conscious mechanosensory threshold, root locomotion, biological diagnosis, measured weight or new injury claimed.
proposals.continuity: Existing Marah macrocarpa perennial with large underground tuber and slender seasonal vines. Existing Point Loma home32.67/-117.24 retained; source is Glendale, compatible species imagery, not proof of travel or a tracked individual. The episode does not require a new neighbor or repeat a coil holding during a gust. She experiences the same leaf load through newly exposed tuber tissue rather than tendril tension. No new avatar or identity.
proposals.leadReview: Lead opened exact image and read literal body. Source is sharp, but a tiny leaf failing to bend a massive tuber is mechanically predictable and creates no consequential response or relationship beyond stated scale. Preserve passage and evidence.
